propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when a model id contains a colon (canonical Bedrock versioned ids like `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` have colons in their version suffix, not as a provider separator).

The qualifier-detection logic treats any colon as evidence of provider-qualification, causing unqualified versioned Bedrock ids to bypass the configured provider and downstream fail with a misleading error naming a fragment of the model id as the provider.
Two independent implementations of the qualification test (`_resolve_target` and `infer_provider`) can drift apart; they must share a single source of truth.
Explicitly configured provider must be checked before any inline qualifier in the model string, so no punctuation can overrule an explicit instruction.
Conflicting provider/qualifier pairs (e.g. `provider="bedrock"` with model `openai:gpt-4o`) must raise an error rather than silently picking a winner.
Both canonical versioned (`...-v1:0`) and unversioned alias Bedrock model forms must work and pass tests, since the unversioned form accidentally passed even against the bug.
